## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The README (or a session-info/colophon file) documents the operating system and version, the statistical software or programming language and version, and, where relevant, hardware (CPU, RAM, cores, GPU/HPC) and expected runtime. Alternatively or additionally, the environment is captured so it can be rebuilt (e.g. a Dockerfile or container image with a pinned base, a virtual machine, or a cloud capsule such as Binder or Code Ocean) and it builds and runs on another machine.
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
Environment information is present but incomplete (e.g. software named without version, operating system missing, no runtime given for long computations); or a container/VM/capsule is provided but cannot be built or run at the point of reproduction.
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No information on the computing environment is given and no captured environment is provided.
:::

[Based on: [#19](../../sources.qmd#p19 "The ReproRubric: evaluation criteria for the reproducibility of computational analyses") three levels (documented with versions / built with a script / VM or container), [#95](../../sources.qmd#p95 "Computational reproducibility in finance: evidence from 1,000 tests") R3 OS + hardware specs, [#14](../../sources.qmd#p14 "An empirical analysis of journal policy effectiveness for computational reproducibility") hardware/system software/processors, [#55](../../sources.qmd#p55 "Computational reproducibility: a practical framework for data curators") in code or README, [#71](../../sources.qmd#p71 "Teaching for Large-Scale Reproducibility Verification") resources summarized in README, [#128](../../sources.qmd#p128 "The reliability of replications: a study in computational reproductions") 'session info', [#40](../../sources.qmd#p40 "The role of containers in reproducibility") pinned base image.]{.source-note}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::
